neighbours.label: a preposition placing a body or object physically on, through or into something ('lay on the bed', 'run through the plaster', 'toss into')
fire: The old man was sleeping on the hospital couch all night.
Stand with your palms pressed flat on the wall.
Copper pipes run through the concrete under the kitchen floor.
Neighbors dump broken chairs and trash into the vacant lot.
Water from the roof drains through a long tube beneath the yard.
The cat climbed onto the shelf and curled up beside the books.
He laid the injured dog gently on a blanket in the truck.
The workers poured wet cement into the deep holes by the road.
quiet: The old man was thinking on the matter all night.
Stand by your decision and rely on your own judgment.
Copper prices rose through the first half of the year.
Neighbors looked into the matter and talked it over.
Word of the plan spread through a long chain of friends.
The cat came home on Friday and slept until the weekend.
He spoke kindly on behalf of the dog's owner in the town.
The workers went into debt during the long strike by the union.

notes: Card: ' on' x9, ' in' x5, ' through' x4, ' onto' x4, ' into' x2, ' enters', ' passes'. Probe: ' through' in 'cables run through the plaster' 0.805; ' on' in 'lay ... on the bed' 0.780; ' on' in 'flat on the floor' 0.733; ' into' 0.526; 'on Monday' 0.056; 'depends on' 0.003; 'through his whole life' 0.070.
